Emery’s turn to make changes: McGinn and Alysson off, Barkley and Hemmings on.

Mbeumo shoots just wide of the far post from 20 yards out, not a bad effort. Villa are not impregnable, but they are managing this half’s two-goal lead better than the first. A touch more compact, and winning fouls to halt any nascent United momentum.

Triple sub by United: Dalot, Amad and Tielemans the players off, replaced by Dorgu, Lacey and Mount. Hearty cheers from Lacey from the United fans, the young attacker who set up Cunha’s winner against Roma.

Huge cheers when Dalot is substituted from the United fans followed by boos as he left the pitch. Shades of Zirkzee against Newcastle.

United work a free-kick short, and Fernandes’s shot from the edge of the box deflects wide. Bodies fall like skittles from the corner, but VAR decides there was nothing sinister in Villa’s defending. Alysson then bodies Mbuemo but the referee waves it away as the home crowd appeal for a decision.

Tielemans slices a left-footed shot over the bar from distance, but both teams are still finding it easy to progress the ball and create half chances. There are surely more goals on the way if it carries on like this.

McGinn with a teasing delivery from the free-kick, and but his cross evaded everyone. Mbuemo then tests Suzuki with a snap shot, but the flag was up for offside against the Manchester United forward in any case.

Attack, or counter-attack, might prove the best form of defence for Villa because Alysson is tearing it up down their right flank. Heaven hacks him down at the expense of a yellow card, and the forward requires some treatment.

Chaotic defending from the free-kick, with Yoro losing his bearings and heading against his own crossbar from a few yards out. There ensues a goal-mouth scramble, but Goretzka was on hand to make sure from a few yards out. United two goals down for the second time in the game. Can they do it all again?

Good work in midfield from McGinn to protect the ball not once but twice and buy a foul from Fernandes, who throws his hands up at the decision. That is the name of the game for Villa: if they can keep the ball for longer spells, chances will open up around the edge of United’s box.

Mazraoui with a misdirected cross that drifts behind for a goal kick. Old Trafford is quiet again, save for the Villa fans in the corner. Maguire has his critics, but his half-time departure has not helped United’s cause. Their defence was flimsy enough with him there.

Just like in the first half, Villa have an early goal. Unerring finish from the spot from McGinn, plenty of power and sending Lammens the wrong way. Can Villa keep their foot on the pedal this time?

John McGinn cooly fires home a penalty to restore Aston Villa's lead two minutes into the second half! 🟣 https://t.co/JGI1KTpEbn

Dalot looks rueful after the referee points to the spot because he knows he has tripped the lively Alysson. The Villa forward has been a menace throughout. John McGinn to take, one week on from his miss against Fulham.

Alysson has been a nightmare for Dalot all game but that was such a lame challenge. You have to wonder how Dalot keeps getting picked.

It appears enforced, with Harry Maguire replaced by Ayden Heaven. United will play the second half with two 20-year-old central defenders.

United have hope again just when things looked completely hopeless. After Aston Villa scored twice in the opening four minutes, thoughts were turning to official club statements and pictures of corner flags.

Carrick’s team have been irrepressible since though, attacking Villa with abandon and scoring two well-deserved goals.

Villa lost their grip too easily with a two-goal lead, and it’s not the first time you can say that about an Emery team.

VAR have a decision to make after a high boot from Fernandes on Alysson in United’s box but the incident is checked and cleared.

Villa miss a chance to go in with a lead, Alysson on the run again and he dinked the ball over Lammens but wide of the far post.

The midfielder has scored against his former club, a shot from the edge of the box squeezing under Suzuki after a well-placed cut-back from Mazraoui down the right. Mbuemo was stood in front of the goalkeeper, but he was onside and the goal stands.

It looked like United’s chance to draw level before half-time had gone when Amad, without a United goal for almost a year, had a shot from a great position saved but Tielemans has equalised after another good attack. United have responded well since Fernandes’ penalty although Villa very nearly went back ahead with Alysson, who has been a menace down United’s left, almost scoring.

Youri Tielemans against his former club! 😱 Manchester United are level just before the break! https://t.co/8kFOQkl814

Big save from Suzuki to deny Amad! Strong hand from the goalkeeper to keep it out and avoid spilling the ball to a United player.

Suzuki called upon to sweep up well outside of his area, before a Fernandes shot hits Mazraoui in the head. Jackson wastes a Villa counter-attack with a careless pass.

Mazraoui penalised for a foul on Manzambi near the corner of the penalty area. Welcome territory, and the chance to push for a third goal before half-time.

Floated in by McGinn, but Torres’s header loops comfortably over the bar.

Maguire and Yoro defend well against Jackson’s peeling run in the left channel before United come forward again through Cunha. The ball is worked across to Amad, who cuts inside Maatsen a little too easily and shoots not far wide of the far post.

The last few minutes of the game have been quieter, welcome news from Villa’s perspective. Jackson, Alysson and Manzambi still look a threat when they have a chance to attack space from deep, but they need more midfield control from Kamara and Goretzka.

Fernandes whips free-kick wide of the post from a crossing position, but feels he should have a corner for a flick off Suzuki. The Old Trafford crowd are up again after Mainoo slides in to win a tackle in midfield.

This is one-way traffic now, United swarming all over Villa and Amad’s deflected shot trickles just wide of Suzuki’s post. United’s response to the first four minutes of the game has been impressive, but Villa are playing a part in their own downfall.

United on top now and have a little momentum after that shocking start. The crowd have also lifted noticeably.

United are certainly in the ascendancy now, Villa allowing too much space around the edge of their box. From there, a Fernandes shot deflects off the boot of John McGinn and loops not far wide of the post. Suzuki palms the ball behind for another corner.

The goalkeeper clears the second corner in unorthodox fashion, before Mainoo’s shot deflects into Suzuki’s gloves.

Cracking effort from Cunha, going for the far corner from 25 yards with a curling shot but Suzuki was equal to it and tipped the ball around the post. From the resulting corner, Aston Villa’s goalkeeper gathers at the second attempt after attempting to catch.

A more chaotic game suits United, Villa will want some more sustained periods of possession. McGinn and Manzambi’s positioning is causing United problems. Mazraoui is stepping out to mark the Swiss but not always getting there. Diligent defending from Amad to track back against Maatsen.

Some fans had been encouraging a walk-out in the 21st minute (to signal 21 years of “decay” under the Glazers”) but if any fans have left it’s very few. Old Trafford still packed.

Villa trying to restore some order with considered passing from deep, but Maguire steps in well to take the ball off McGinn. Mbemo is the flagged for offside. United are the team with bigger problems, but Villa do not look wholly trustworthy themselves.

The slow, stuttered run up pays off this time as Fernandes waits for Suzuki to dive right, before passing the ball the other way. Game on.

A lifeline for Man Utd! 🔥 Bruno Fernandes converts from the penalty spot to reduce the defecit! https://t.co/wy7L1iAhbx

Kamara penalised for lunging at Cunha in the penalty from the wrong side, and his left leg caught the United man before he got to the ball. Not particularly contentions, but VAR is taking time to check. Decision confirmed.

Lindelof clears Cunha’s cross. “You should have signed for a big club!” is the chant from Villa’s away end, aimed at Youri Tielemans.

Then Manzambi releases Jackson into space, Villa’s centre-forward galloping into space but Yoro did well to slow him down and avoid pulling a shirt at the expense of a corner.

Fernandes then drags a snap shot wide of the post. Frantic stuff.

2 - After three minutes and 40 seconds, this is the earliest Manchester United have ever been 2-0 down in a Premier League game. Slumber. https://t.co/76iMwVLhTK

Villa continue to pour forward with menace, United’s defence offering all the resistance of wet tissue paper. I’m not sure I can recall a home team starting a match this badly, perhaps Spurs vs Fulham last season runs it close.

The sheer scale of the incompetence is staggering. Two goals down in three minutes and 40 seconds, shambolic defending all round, dismal goalkeeping, boos echoing around after that second Villa goes in, the ownership targeted at every opportunity. “You’re getting sacked in the morning” the Villa fans sing at Michael Carrick. And now “Unai’s right, you’re f------ s----”, a nod to Emery being heavily linked with the Old Trafford job but close to signing a new deal with Villa. Tielemans is being taunted with chants of “You used to play for a big club” and “you sold your soul for this s---hole”.

These scenes are truly surreal, Manchester United are 2-0 down inside four minutes. This is a new low.

It was a meat and drink free-kick floated into the box, the ball dropped for Alysson to hit from the edge of the box, and Lammens could only parry back into danger.

Jackson was free as a bird to score from a few yards, and he was well onside.

Nicolas Jackson has made it 2-0 to Aston Villa after just 4 minutes and boos ring out around Old Trafford 🤯 https://t.co/G7oWDNMjGS

Bright play from Villa who are first to every ball, working the ball with sharpness across the box from right to left, and Alysson takes his shot first time and it creeps under the body of Lammens.

What a start for Aston Villa! 🔥 Alysson fires home to give the the visitors the lead https://t.co/F0nfSRMWRa

Villa get the game under way, and they have turned United around. The home team will kick towards the Stretford End in the first half.

Green and gold balloons galore on the Stretford End. Remembrance Sunday will be marked before kick-off with the Last Post and a minute’s silence.

United fans have paraded a new banner in the Stretford End that reads: “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners.” Hundreds of green and gold balloons are again being released – a nod to the club’s original colours and a symbol of protest. Lots of anti Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe chants again reverberating with the co-owners told to: “Sell United and f--- off home”.

It’s not the only banner. One reads: “History, Dignity, Integrity, You Stole It All”. Another read “Jim Ain’t The One”. One simply says: “Sell Up.”

"We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners" #MUFC #AVFC https://t.co/6maQckC0qm

Taylor Harwood-Bellis starts at the back for Villa, and his father-in-law Roy Keane is in the Sky Sports studio.

"I don't want to be too harsh on him after the game" 😅 Roy Keane hopes his son-in-law Taylor Harwood-Bellis plays well for Aston Villa today! https://t.co/lS9AjOkSBj

They will kick-off in 19th, two points adrift of safety. Sunderland’s win over Chelsea lifts them above United, but Palace are now bottom after a 3-1 home defeat by Liverpool.

This “Glazers Out, Ratcliffe Out” flag is being passed around on the forecourt outside Old Trafford.

One fan group is calling for supporters to walk out in the 21st minute in protest at 21 years of Glazer ownership.

Once upon a time, the only Old Trafford flyers on the agenda were Ryan Giggs and Andrei Kanchelskis. Not so today.

Unai Emery has picked a surprising back four, it could end up being a situational back three of Lindelof, Harwood-Bellis and Torres when Maatsen raids forward from left-back. Villa fans are keen to see more of Mbaye, their summer signing from PSG, but he has to settle for a place on the bench.

With Lisandro Martinez suspended, Yoro moves inside from right-back to partner Maguire. Dalot annd Mazraoui can play full-back on both sides. No Carlos Baleba after his hamstring injury, so the Tielemans-Mainoo-Fernandes trio has another chance to convince. United's starting XI to face Aston Villa 🔴📋 ➡️ Youri Tielemans and Nous Mazraoui ⬅️ Carlos Baleba and Ayden Heaven 💪 @PatrickDorgu13 returns to the bench https://t.co/w24eW6tO2b

With four Premier League games in progress the picture is ever-changing, but United are currently 19th in the Premier League table. The club, famously, were relegated in 1974 with the coup de grâce applied by Denis Law’s backheel when the Scot was playing in a City shirt. In this piece, James Ducker looks back on the previous occasions when one of the world’s biggest clubs has flirted with calamity.

When Villa dropped into the Championship, it did not change the fact they were the biggest club in the Midlands. No matter what Tom Brady does at Birmingham City, that’s not changing any time soon. They sought and achieved promotion by raiding Brentford.

Nobody was complaining about a sleeping giant taking Dean Smith, Ezri Konsa or Ollie Watkins and potentially stalling Brentford’s progression.

Nor was it suggested hiring Emery from Villarreal was an odd move given that the Spanish side had recently won the Europa League and reached the latter stages of the Champions League.

Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence. More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership. Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

Tottenham Hotspur star Pedro Porro is a target for both Real Madrid and Barcelona - and appears to be heading back to Spain

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Tottenham Hotspur full-back Pedro Porro has opened up about leaving N17 once again.

The World Cup winner signed a new deal with the Lilywhites over the summer to keep him in North London until 2031, after back-to-back 17th-place finishes in the Premier League.

After well-documented interest from Spanish giants, the Tottenham man has opened up to boldly tell reporters “it's true” he will return to his homeland, as Real Madrid and Barcelona circle for his signature.

In comments relayed by Sport Witness, Porro has opened up once again to link himself away from Spurs.

The outlet records this as the sixth time that the Spaniard has spoken about moving – despite the implication that he's talking about his long-term future – with Porro even prefacing his comments this time with, “I don’t want to get into any trouble”.

“I’ve just renewed my contract with Tottenham,” Porro began, “I have a great deal of respect for my club, and I’m very grateful for the support they give me.

“It’s true, and no secret, that I hope to return to Spain one day, as it’s my home country. But first and foremost, I want to emphasise my respect for the club I’m currently under contract with. As for the future, well, we’ll see.”

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

As long ago as March, the 27-year-old spoke of a “dream” when asked about Real Madrid interest, while most recently, he called Barcelona president Joan Laporte's praise of him “flattering” and said, “I’m focused on the national team now, and then we’ll see.”

Real were initially linked with a move for Porro towards the back end of last season but after purchasing Denzel Dumfries to compete with Trent Alexander-Arnold – and manager Jose Mourinho deploying Federico Valverde at full-back, too – it appears as if the door has closed on Porro moving to the Bernabeu for now.

Barça, meanwhile, have their own defensive issues with Jules Kounde currently out injured – while La Masia duo Brian Farinas and Xavi Espart have both started at right-back for boss Hansi Flick.

With Ronald Araujo on loan at Liverpool and Kounde linked with an exit over the summer, there is certainly potential for the Blaugrana to shop for a new right-back in the coming months.

Whether Porro really is talking about returning to Spain now or in the distant future will surely become apparent, should Barça come calling for his services.

The Spurs man is worth €45 million, according to Transfermarkt. Spurs host Ipswich Town when Premier League action resumes after the international break.

#1061. Fifa loses court bid to block Uefa probe into Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Gianni Infantino abandoned his World Cup sell-off plan just days after it was made public

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Legal efforts by Fifa to prevent Uefa from securing disclosure documents from Thrive Capital and JP Morgan have been thrown out by a court in New York. The order centres on the collapsed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

The project, spearheaded by Fifa president Gianni Infantino, aimed to manage commercial interests for the World Cup and other tournaments by offering private investors a minority stake. It was abandoned in August following rejection by three continental confederations.

Uefa had threatened to boycott Fifa competitions and, last month, demanded answers regarding a series of questions about FFE and broader concerns under Infantino’s presidency.

Those enquiries focused on the decision to give exclusivity to Thrive Capital to lead the group of private investors. Thrive was established by Joshua Kushner, the brother of United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law.

JP Morgan was also confirmed by Fifa to be working alongside it on FFE, having previously acted as financial backers for the doomed European Super League project in 2021.

Thursday’s judgment in Manhattan means Fifa’s motion to intervene has been rejected, although it is understood another court decision is required to grant the release of documents.

Judge Jeannette Vargas wrote: "The court has already decided that the US Fifa parties have no direct, substantial and legally protectable interest in the subject matter of this application.

"In light of this determination, the court exercises its discretion to decline leave to intervene."

Furthermore, Fifa insists that the ruling has not ordered the explicit disclosure of documents, such as those related to FFE, with the world footballing governing body putting out a statement addressing such reports.

“Reports that Fifa’s opposition to Uefa’s application for disclosure has been dismissed are inaccurate,” a statement read.

“Neither Fifa nor any other entity has been ordered to produce documents. Today’s ruling concerned the motion by Fifa’s US subsidiaries to intervene in the actions brought by Uefa against Thrive and JP Morgan.

“The Court has not addressed the merits of Uefa’s application and no documents are required to be produced.”

The ruling comes ahead of March’s Fifa election, with Infantino set to run as he seeks a fourth term as president.

Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association (JFA), announced last week that he would run for the presidency.

Meanwhile, former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is also considering putting himself forward as a candidate to challenge Infantino.

Wenger is not currently viewed as the preferred candidate for Uefa, with other individuals also under evaluation. It is understood he remains undecided over whether to launch a bid.

Wenger’s reputation within football and intimate knowledge of the Fifa administration would render him a formidable challenger to Infantino should he choose to stand, with the Frenchman having served as Fifa’s chief of global football development since 2019.

Former Southampton and Manchester United midfielder Morgan Schneiderlin explains why he thinks Mauricio Pochettino will be a success at Old Trafford

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Manchester United look set to change manager following a run of just one win in 10 league matches under Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino is in the picture to replace Carrick, meanwhile former Old Trafford and Southampton midfielder Morgan Schneiderlin has delivered an emphatic endorsement of the Argentine coach.

Pochettino is widely considered the leading candidate to take charge, and Schneiderlin - who played the finest football of his career under the Argentine at St Mary’s Stadium - insists the 54-year-old has the personal qualities required to unify a fractured club.

Reflecting on Pochettino’s arrival in English football in 2013, Schneiderlin revealed that an initial language barrier did nothing to dilute the manager’s authority.

"He didn't need to speak a lot of the language," Schneiderlin recalls, via Comeon.com. "He would put an arm around you, and with the translator or someone who spoke English, he’d explain what he liked about you and exactly what he wanted you to do.

"I'll always remember his team talk before that first game against Everton. He was just screaming in Spanish, a deeply motivational speech, entirely in Spanish, but all we could hear and understand was: 'Press like lions! Press like lions! Press like lions!' And we did press like lions!

"Now that he speaks fluent English, it's going to be even easier for him. But his charisma, his presence, and the way he carried himself - we were just under his spell straight away."

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That buy-in was cemented on the Saints' training ground, where Pochettino instituted a relentless physical culture.

"We were working very, very hard in training sessions and in the gym, not to be bodybuilders or look nice on the beach, but building a lot of lower-body strength," Schneiderlin explains.

"He used me much more as a true box-to-box midfielder - he wanted me to run, to press, and to win the ball back. It was very enjoyable."

However, Schneiderlin has warned against expecting Pochettino to instantly rely on academy graduates to dig Man United out of trouble, stressing that Old Trafford 'demands results immediately' and requires a stable footing first.

Having since managed Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, Pochettino will set foot inside Old Trafford a more battle-hardened version of the coach who took charge at Southampton 13 years ago.

"He arrives now with so much experience behind him and so much baggage, both good and bad, he has learned from," Schneiderlin added. "He will use everything he learned from being in Paris Saint-Germain dealing with big players and big personalities."

#1059. Morgan Rogers hits back at criticism of Cole Palmer’s commitment to England: ‘It’s a lie’

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Palmer missed out on the England squad for the November internationals with Thomas Tuchel saying ‘he misses too many opportunities to impress’

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Morgan Rogers has leapt to the defence of Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer by asserting that it is “a lie” to question whether he is committed to the England cause.

Palmer was left out of the England squad by Thomas Tuchel once again for the November internationals, with the England coach saying “he misses too many opportunities to impress” after withdrawing from the previous camp with a minor injury.

The Chelsea forward was also one of the notable absentees from England’s roster for the 2026 World Cup.

Rogers, who scored in Thursday’s 2-1 win over Croatia, has hit back at any suggestion that Palmer’s struggle for favour is down to his devotion to the national team.

Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live: “It’s a lie. He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

“We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he’s been managing the injuries ever since.

“He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn’t feel 100 per cent himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn’t?

“But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10, 15 years. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then you have to fully support it. It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England.

“It’s a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don’t get it and he doesn’t get it. I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.”

Palmer was one of five withdrawals at the start of the last camp, with Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Tino Livramento and Marcus Rashford also pulling out.

Rice is the only one of that quintet recalled as Tuchel reiterated that he will always give preference to those who “walk the talk”.

Rogers nevertheless hopes to see Palmer, who has started every Chelsea game this season, return to the fold “sooner rather than later”.

“Of course I do,” Rogers added. “What a player he is. What a person he is and it’s someone you want to see in an England shirt.

“He’s got so much quality, so much ability. We all know what he can do, what he’s done, so of course we want to see him in an England shirt and hopefully sooner rather than later.”

Rogers’ passionate defence of Palmer was put to Tuchel in his post-match press conference.

“It’s totally fine,” the England boss said. “He’s his team-mate and I guess his friend, so why wouldn’t he? Why wouldn’t he make an emotional statement if he did it?

“I didn’t hear it, so I will not comment on it. All I can say is I was very happy with the emotional commitment from Morgan and the physical commitment of Morgan Rogers.

“I think he was the standout player today, offensively and defensively, and that’s what matters.”

Mauricio Pochettino took over at Southampton back in 2013 and has gone on to manage some of the world's biggest clubs since

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Mauricio Pochettino’s managerial career in English football first materialised because Southampton officials travelled to Spain to scout Philippe Coutinho, the Argentine revealed in an exclusive interview with FourFourTwo earlier this year.

With Pochettino now heavily linked with and expected to take over the Manchester United post, more light is being shed on the 52-year-old's initial move to the Premier League.

In January 2013, Southampton dismissed Nigel Adkins despite the club sitting in relative safety following back-to-back promotions. Chairman Nicola Cortese appointed Pochettino, who had left Espanyol two months earlier. The connection, however, was made while Cortese and sporting director Paul Mitchell were running checks on Coutinho, who was on loan at the Catalan side from Inter Milan, and would later complete an £8.5 million transfer to Liverpool.

"In England, nobody knew who I was," Pochettino said. "[Former Southampton chairman] Nicola Cortese is another key figure in my career. They were tracking Philippe Coutinho, who was on loan with us at Espanyol, and came to a match.

"Both Nicola and the sporting director, Paul Mitchell, became interested in the way I coached and expressed myself on the touchline. Six months later, they called me to take the job. Nicola took a real gamble – he had the courage to make that appointment because the club was in a comfortable position in the Premier League, having achieved back-to-back promotions. It was a risky move for him, but he also knew what we were capable of doing."

Pochettino's arrival at St Mary’s was initially met with scepticism in the English press due to the timing of Adkins’ sacking, particularly given he initially conducted post-match interviews in Spanish with the help of a translator. However, the Argentine explained that a language barrier helped shield him from the immediate fallout.

"Not at all," Pochettino said when asked if the reaction generated any undue pressure. "We were young and full of confidence. I had the advantage of not speaking English at the beginning, so I wasn’t reading or listening to anything – I paid no attention to the media.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I was a bit isolated from everything, living in my own bubble. My assistant Jesus Perez acted as a filter and only told me what was truly important."

Pochettino quickly implemented an aggressive, high-pressing system on the south coast, leaning heavily on young domestic talent including current Man United defender Luke Shaw and future Liverpool midfielder Adam Lallana.

"We had players who were physically like jets, perfectly suited to how we wanted to play – a style built on aggression and intensity," Pochettino said.

"Technically they were good, but the best thing was their potential to improve even further. We were a perfect match.

"In England, the ones who began to introduce a different kind of football were Brendan Rodgers at Liverpool and us at Southampton, with our build-up and high attacking press."

With Man United's hierarchy holding talks over Michael Carrick's position following a return of one win from ten league games, Pochettino is very much in the frame to be the next man up. For a manager now positioned to take over at Old Trafford, his initial entry into English football remains tied to a scouting trip for an ex-Liverpool star.

#1057. Sydney Swans players will not face charges over hotel sexual assault investigation, police say

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Three women are pursuing civil action against players

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Four players of the Australian Football League (AFL) who were under scrutiny over an alleged sexual assault at a Melbourne hotel will not face any charges due to insufficient evidence.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Nick Blakey – the Sydney Swans players – were under investigation since late August by Victoria police over the alleged sexual assault at the Pullman Hotel.

One of the women at the centre of allegations against the players has been left devastated by the outcome, her lawyer said.

“Following a thorough investigation and based on legal advice, Victoria Police will not proceed with criminal charges due to insufficient evidence,” a police statement read.

“Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment.”

Some adult entertainers were believed to have joined the players at the hotel after being hired following the Swans' win against Essendon on 17 August.

Police previously said that three women, believed to be adult entertainers, alleged inappropriate touching during the incident in the early hours of that day.

At least one woman was seen leaving the hotel room in a distressed state with a call made to the emergency Triple Zero line soon after.

The four players, along with teammate Riley Bice, were suspended by the Swans for breaching the club’s standards, including drinking and bringing women back to their hotel after the game.

The players have denied any wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking.

Slater and Gordon senior lawyer Jackson Pannam, the firm representing one of the women who reported the alleged sexual assault, said the decision not to charge the men did not mean the alleged acts did not happen.

“Our client is devastated by this outcome,” Mr Pannam said. “She reported the incident immediately, provided a formal statement and cooperated fully with the investigation. She has shown enormous courage in coming forward.

“The absence of criminal charges does not prevent a civil claim from proceeding. This outcome also sits within broader patterns of underreporting and attrition in sexual offence matters.”

John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers who is representing two other women, said their clients were "very disappointed and distressed" over the outcome.

"My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said.

Sydney Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich addressed a press conference on Friday, saying it was a difficult period for everyone involved and affected by the hotel incident.

"We appreciate and understand that everyone has been dealing with it in their own way, and we thank them for their support during that time," he said.

"We've been in constant contact with the players through the whole process.

"Today's a moment for them to move forward. It's a time for everyone to move forward, and at some point, they'll be back here at training, back with their teammates, and that's going to be an important step."

Sydney Swans management said they stand by their decision to expel the player. It is "because their conduct fell short of the standards of behaviour expected at the club".

"The club was clear from the outset that this decision was separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision.

"The club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," the statement said.

Mr Blakey last month joined North Melbourne football club and apologised for "the events that led up to my exit from Sydney".

"I know I have to win back the trust of the broader community, football and otherwise," he said at the time.

The 2026 NWSL Championship is just two games away, with four teams remaining in the race for the title.

Reigning champions Gotham FC are still in contention after edging past Seattle Reign, while Washington Spirit, Kansas City Current and Utah Royals have also booked their places in the semi-finals.

With the final four now confirmed, two intriguing matchups await on November 14 and 15, as the teams battle for a place in the Championship match in Washington.

The 2026 NWSL playoffs began last weekend with the top eight teams battling it out for a place in the semi-finals, following a regular season in which Gotham FC emerged as the team to beat.

The defending champions finished top of the standings to claim the NWSL Shield for a first time and secure the No. 1 seed, while Washington Spirit, San Diego Wave, Kansas City Current, Angel City, Portland Thorns, Utah Royals and Seattle Reign also booked their places.

The first three quarter-finals were all decided by a single goal. Utah Royals pulled off the biggest upset, beating second seeds San Diego Wave 1-0 to secure their first-ever post-season victory.

Kansas City Current also edged through, with Michelle Cooper converting an extra-time penalty to seal a 1-0 win over Angel City.

Gotham also needed just one goal to overcome Seattle Reign, with an early own goal from Jordyn Bugg proving decisive.

Washington Spirit, meanwhile, delivered the standout performance of the round, sweeping aside Portland Thorns 4-1. Trinity Rodman scored twice, while Clara Luvanga contributed a goal and two assists.

The semi-final line-up is now confirmed, with Washington hosting Utah on November 14 before Gotham take on Kansas City the following day. The winners will meet in the Championship final at Audi Field on November 21.

Shaw has been one of Gotham's most influential attacking players this season, leading the team with 11 goals and five assists. The 21-year-old can create moments of brilliancem, through her movement, dribbling or eye for goal. Having returned from injury to start the quarter-final against Seattle, her availability and fitness could be particularly important as Gotham look to defend their title.

While Temwa Chawinga will often steal the headlines, Bethune has also enjoyed an outstanding season at Kansas City, setting a new NWSL single-season record with 11 assists. The midfielder's creativity and ability to unlock opposition defences will be crucial against a Gotham side that conceded just 23 goals during the regular season. With two-time MVP Chawinga providing a constant attacking threat beside her, KC Current's attacking line is one to be feared.

Rodman has been central to Washington's success this season, recording a career-best 12 goals and eight assists in the regular season. The forward carried that form into the quarter-finals, scoring twice and providing an assist in the 4-1 victory over Portland. Named an NWSL MVP finalist, she will be one of the biggest threats for Utah to contain.

Lacasse has been one of Utah's most productive players this season, contributing eight goals and 10 assists in the regular campaign. Her ability to create chances as well as find the net will be vital if the Royals are to continue their impressive play-off run. The 33-year-old played a key role in their quarter-final victory over second seeds San Diego Wave, providing the assist for Kiana Palacios' winning goal and Utah will be hoping she can help them produce another upset against Washington Spirit.

Prediction: Washington Spirit 3-1 Utah Royals

Utah have already shown they should not be underestimated, eliminating second seeds San Diego Wave away from home. Their defensive organisation and ability to take their chances make them a dangerous opponent.

However, Washington will be full of confidence after their emphatic quarter-final victory over Portland. With Trinity Rodman in outstanding form and the backing of a home crowd at Audi Field, they should have enough attacking quality to reach another Championship final...which is also to be played at Audi Field.

Prediction: Gotham FC 1-2 Kansas City Current

While defending champions Gotham finished the regular season with the league's best defensive record, conceding just 23 goals in 30 matches, Kansas City have the attacking firepower to trouble any side in the league.

Bethune's creativity and Chawinga's threat in front of goal will test Gotham's defence, while Kansas City's ability to score from different areas makes them particularly difficult to contain. Gotham's experience of winning on the biggest stage cannot be overlooked, but Kansas City have the quality to end the reigning champions' hopes of back-to-back titles.

#1054. Thomas Tuchel disappointed with England fans booing Ben White: ‘I thought we were past that’

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The Arsenal defender has not been allowed to forget his departure from the 2022 World Cup squad

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Thomas Tuchel is confident a resilient Ben White can cope with the boo boys but hopes England fans will allow the defender to start a new chapter.

The 29-year-old made himself unavailable for the national team under Sir Gareth Southgate having left Qatar during the knockout phase of the 2022 World Cup for “personal reasons”.

White reportedly fell out with former assistant Steve Holland and only returned to the England set-up under Tuchel in March, when he was booed by fans before missing the World Cup through injury.

The Arsenal defender this week said supporters would not react like that if they knew the full story, but he refused to “throw anyone under the bus” and was jeered having been brought on in Thursday’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia.

Put to Tuchel that even Croatian substitute Luka Modric got a warmer reception than England introduction White, he said with a laugh: “I didn’t hear the boos, to be honest.

“I heard the claps for Luka Modric, which is nice because he deserves it, he’s a legend of the game, but I honestly didn’t hear the boos for Ben. I thought we were past that chapter.

“I hope it doesn’t happen again. He’s a player of ours. Since I’m in charge, he’s desperate to come and to be with the group. He doesn’t put a foot wrong since I’m in charge.

“I can only judge him on what I see and what I experienced, and it is on the highest level, and he can really help us to win football matches.

“Like I said, he’s part of our group, and we will protect our group, and are protective of our group. He deserves to be with us and, yeah, I hope we can open a new chapter for him.”

There were fewer boos than in March’s friendlies and Tuchel is confident such a reaction will not see White walk away again should negativity continue.

“I don’t think so,” he said. “I don’t want to make it bigger than it is. I don’t think so, I don’t hope so.

“He seemed to me always committed and always dedicated and excited to come into camp and get the call-up.

“He had too many injuries. He’s a high-quality player, and I honestly don’t even know what happened and what were the deep reasons in the situation that he left camp.

“So, like I said, (since) I’m in charge, there is no reason to doubt his commitment or passion. I don’t want to think in these extreme terms at the moment.

“He overcame the boos the last time. I didn’t hear them this time and he can play on a high level. He proves it week in, week out for Arsenal.”

The White situation was a sideshow on a night that saw Harry Kane cap his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a match-winning penalty after Morgan Rogers’ goal was cancelled out by Petar Sucic.

The 2-1 win rubber-stamped their place in March’s Nations League quarter-finals and keeps hopes alive of topping Group A3 ahead of Sunday’s trip to leaders Spain.

Tuchel said: “It cannot always be glamorous and super exciting. Sometimes just to be serious and determined, and we got the job done.

“We wanted the win, we wanted a ‘final’ on Sunday in Spain, and we have it.”

#1052. Harry Kane hints at playing two more World Cups for England after Luka Modric inspiration

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The England captain has no plans to slow down after reaching a landmark 126 caps

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Harry Kane has pledged to "push the limits" of his career, taking motivation from 41-year-old Luka Modric after breaking the men's England appearance record against Croatia.

The 33-year-old captain experienced a memorable evening at a sold-out Wembley Stadium on Thursday, where a giant tifo proclaimed ‘England’s finest’ as he led out the team for his landmark 126th cap.

Kane received a rapturous reception from the crowd and presented the Ballon d’Or on the pitch prior to a series of presentations commemorating his new men's caps record.

The Prince of Wales and previous record holder Peter Shilton led the pre-match tributes, on a night that culminated in the skipper scoring a penalty to secure a 2-1 Nations League victory over Croatia.

"It was incredible, just everything was amazing," Kane said, having admitted he was "trying to play it cool" when walking out to the banner recognising his achievement.

"A big thank you to everyone who organised it here at the FA, with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka (Modric) and the Croatian organisation for their gift as well.

"Obviously I knew there was going to be something before the game and it was just a special moment.

"It’s been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening and of course it’s an important moment in our history as a national team, so you have to enjoy these moments.

"But then once the game started, it was just full focus on that. I’ve said before, these occasions feel much better when you win and obviously now I can take a breath and enjoy the whole night itself."

Kane remained on the Wembley pitch long after the final whistle alongside friends and family, who will surely have more historic moments to celebrate in the future.

The forward sits just eight goals short of reaching 100 international strikes and intends to represent England for as long as possible, inspired by fellow Ballon d’Or winner Modric.

The 41-year-old extended his own Croatian caps record to 207 after appearing as a substitute at Wembley, where he received a warm reception from home supporters.

"He’s an inspiration for a lot of us," Kane said. "What an incredible player, but what a great person as well and someone who’s looked after himself.

"A great professional and to be playing 40, 41 now, still at this level, is credit to all of his hard work and his mentality.

"So, yeah, that inspires me to push the limits. Like with him, I think you just keep going to see how far your body takes you, your mentality takes you.

"Everyone’s journey is different for sure but I’ve said before that as long as I feel like I can help the national team, as long as I feel like I’m performing at the highest level, then I’ll be here for as long as I can.

"Whether that’s until I’m 40 or not, we’ll have to wait and see. But right now, yeah, I’ve enjoyed every moment."

Kane's focus now shifts to England's last match of the year against World Cup champions Spain in Madrid, having guaranteed safe passage to the Nations League quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel’s side opened Group A3 with a 3-2 defeat at Wembley, but four consecutive wins since have positioned them with a chance of claiming top spot on Sunday.

"There were things that we can improve on, but it was just about getting the win ultimately," Kane added. "It sets up a fantastic game on Sunday now."

#1051. Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night

One day it will have to end for Harry Kane, but for now, almost 12 years into his England life, there is still no matching the wisdom and influence he has accumulated over all those games and all those goals for his country.

This would have been a great night by any measure for a man collecting his record-breaking 126th England cap. There was a handshake from Peter Shilton, now deposed as king of caps, and a flourish by Kane of his recently acquired Ballon d’Or, once his four children had accompanied him on to the pitch. These are the nights of which dreams are made, and yet – given the defining feature of Kane’s career – there was one more thing to accomplish.

That was a goal from the man who has ploughed relentlessly past the two great England individual landmarks of caps and goals. His second-half penalty won the game and, although he is not infallible from the spot, he is as close to that status as England have ever had. Age has not yet run him down, he can still bend the game to his will, and when it comes to the pressure moments, his longevity seems to offer the upper hand.

This was always going to be Kane’s night, with a great banner on the west side of the stadium paying tribute to the England captain. The Prince of Wales was in attendance for the occasion, too. Luka Modric presented his former Tottenham Hotspur team-mate with a keepsake from the Croatian football federation. Kane had to wait for the second half for the most valuable offering of all.

After the hour, the Danish referee Morten Krogh was advised by his VAR Bastian Dankert to take a second look at a corner tangle involving Jarell Quansah, and decided to award the second-half penalty from which Kane scored. It was certainly clumsy, but these grapples have been overlooked by referees in the past. The 27th successfully converted penalty of the Kane England era followed, and the man himself played the full game.

That was a nod to Modric, a second-half substitute at the age of 41 and now on 207 caps for Croatia and almost 1,200 senior games. This Croatia team still seem unable to part company with their greatest player, despite his struggles against England in the seven-goal defeat in Rijeka. On this occasion, Croatia were much better.

“It was a tight match – a tough one,” Thomas Tuchel, the England manager, said. “We didn’t take our chances when we had chances, so it stayed a tight match. It cannot be glamorous and super-exciting [all the time]. It has to be serious and determined. We wanted a final on Sunday in Spain and we have that.”

The win means that England’s game in Madrid on Sunday against Spain, who beat the Czech Republic and lead the Nations League group by three points, has some bite to it. Another England win would mean they would overtake Spain on goal difference and win the group ahead of the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

This was one game when the players might have wondered if they were due more from a Wembley crowd that went through the motions in the first half and scarcely returned for the second. For the first hour, England dominated a Croatia side who often invited six blue shirts into their back line. Tuchel said his decision to select Dan Burn in the left-sided centre-half position over the left-footed Jarrad Branthwaite was almost split – a “51 per cent decision”.

England would break through just once, when Rogers got enough of his laces on an awkward Jude Bellingham cross deflected behind him and the shot brushed Josko Gvardiol on the way in.

Trent Alexander-Arnold started his third England game of the autumn and the right-back spent most of it in midfield. Not just central midfield, or right midfield, but he also emerged in the inside-left position at times. Kane stepped into the No 10 role when he saw fit and his passing was reliably excellent. From the left it was his pass to Bellingham on the right wing that prefaced the cross for the Rogers goal.

The catastrophe of the defeat last month for Croatia meant they were naturally conservative. Nevertheless, in Martin Baturina, the 23-year-old Como attacking midfielder, they have another fine talent. When Modric did come on, he was applauded on all sides of Wembley. The home fans would later boo the arrival of Ben White, still not forgiven for his 2022 mid-tournament World Cup departure.

Three minutes later it was judged a foul on Quansah by Ivan Smolcic when he pulled the Englishman down and the referee Krogh eventually gave the penalty.

Kane scored that and the substitute James Garner had a goal disallowed in the closing stages of the game, which were much less comfortable for England.

England manager Thomas Tuchel, speaking to ITV: “Good win. We wanted this win desperately and I think we deserved it. I think it was hard work against a good opponent. It took us a while to grow into the game but after 15 minutes I think we did OK, got the goal and got better and more confident and had some good actions and good chances, good half-chances.

“Got a little bit sloppy at the very end of the first half, started the second half very good, didn’t score the second goal, conceded from a set piece, and then showed a good reaction.

“We got the job done and it was important because it was a special occasion for Harry [Kane] and he scored the winner, so perfect evening.”

On whether England were sloppy when they conceded: “It was maybe only three or four minutes before we gave passes away and especially in a moment when we were clearly the better team, we came with a very strong reaction after the half-time, had a beautiful chance created from Declan Rice and they blocked it on the line. It was like our third goal was coming and we had some easy ball losses in our own half that killed our momentum.

“An awkward moment in our box can always happen. It’s important to react and we did it.”

On his defenders: “Good. It was demanding for Dan Burn and also for Jarell [Quansah] because they [Croatia] play with a back five and have two number 10s in between the lines.

“It was a lot of work to do, a lot of communication but they did very well.”

On what will be better against Spain on Sunday: “I don’t know. Everything will be different. Completely different scenario, completely different setup, but I’m very positive that we will get what we want.”

England put in an the-Lord-Mayor’s-show performance following their 7-0 victory over Croatia. But it was still good enough to beat the same opponents 2-1 on the night Harry Kane celebrated his 126th record-breaking cap at Wembley.

Kane capped the night with the winning goal from the penalty spot, but a poor second-half showing – after Morgan Rogers had opened the scoring in the 24th minute – allowed Petar Sucic to equalise, aided by a dreadful mistake by Jarell Quansah.

England captain Harry Kane, speaking to ITV: “An incredible gesture, reception at the start of the game. Once the game starts, it’s about getting the win, getting the three points. We’re playing against a tough team, a team that wanted to prove something tonight.

“I think for large spells of the game we done well. Got a little bit tired towards the end but overall a really great win and sets up a great game on Sunday now.”

On how he was feeling as he stepped up for his penalty: “Same as ever. I missed my last one for Bayern, so I think it’s always important to try and bounce back with the next one. Try to not miss two in a row but executing. I practised yesterday like I always do and it’s just about going out there and doing it out on the pitch.

“I think we gave away a few too many easy balls, especially in our own half, which killed the momentum a little bit. I think we had enough chances to score two or three but we’re playing against a good team.

“We’re in the midst of a run of tough games for club and country, so you can’t always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday, but ultimately it’s about getting a win tonight.”

On aiming to beat Spain and top the group: “100%. After the first game when we lost here against them, we knew we left a bit out there. We knew we could’ve done a bit better. Shortly before kick-off, Croatia captain Luka Modric will present England captain Harry Kane with a special gift from the Croatian Football Federation (HNS), marking his Ballon d’Or win and his achievement in becoming England’s all-time record appearance holder with 126 caps.

Modric is not in the starting line-up but the 41-year-old has 206 caps for his country and will present Kane with a specially crafted replica of the first football ever brought to Croatia, which English industrialists introduced to the town of Zupanja in 1880. This event is regarded as the beginning of organised football on Croatian soil.

England’s 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic last month left them on nine points after four Nations League group games.

It came after a 2-0 win in the away contest, a 7-0 thumping of Croatia and a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

A draw tonight will be enough for Thomas Tuchel’s side to book their place in the quarter-finals of the competition.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

The two worst sides to finish bottom are automatically relegated, while the other bottom sides and third-placed sides are at risk of relegation via a play-off.

Few expect Jobe to be better than his older brother. While Jobe will make his England debut just two months after turning 21, Jude’s first cap came aged 17. By the time that he was Jobe’s age now, Jude had already thrived for England in two international tournaments. But Jobe has one major sporting advantage: he is the younger sibling.

Younger siblings have significantly more chance of becoming elite athletes. If two siblings both become professional, the little sibling is significantly more likely to enjoy the better career.

Jude and Jobe Bellingham could become the first brothers to start for England since Gary and Phil Neville took to the field together 19 years ago, with Jobe included in his first senior squad.

Jack and Bobby Charlton are the only other brothers to play together for England in the post-war period.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the FA’s England app as he discussed his call-up.

“It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great. To be called up for England is a dream itself and I’ve been so proud to have the opportunity to represent England at every age group.

“I always enjoyed coming away with England, I love competing against top players at whichever age group. But to have that chance of an opportunity to represent England with my brother, it’s really hard to put into words.

“I don’t have the words, really. I think it’s only emotion that could describe it, and, hopefully, if that time does come, you’ll see a lot of emotion from people, and definitely from my family.”

There will be a special pre-match presentation to honour Harry Kane becoming England’s record appearance maker, with 126 caps, overtaking Peter Shilton. Shilton has held the record since 1989.

“I think I maybe underappreciated how big it was going to be, how big the reaction was going to be,” he told the BBC.

#1050. England in losing habit after 'failing to adapt' in Perth drubbing

England bowled out for 131 in 33.4 overs as part of seven-wicket drubbing by Australia in first ODI of three-match series at Optus Stadium; second match takes place in Adelaide on Sunday before concluding in Hobart, Wednesday - start times 3.30am, UK time

England "weren't quick enough to adapt to the conditions" as they slumped to a seven-wicket loss to Australia in the first ODI of their three-match series in Perth, according to head coach Brendon McCullum.

Unlike their inadequate preparations for the Ashes Test tour last winter - which also started with a heavy defeat at the Optus Stadium - the tourists this time played a proper warm-up game at the comparably bouncey WACA in Perth, but despite the time spent acclimatising, they were bundled out for a mere 131 in 33.4 overs in the series opener.

"It all happened pretty quick!" McCullum told TNT Sports after his side's heavy defeat, Australia knocking off the runs in 23.3 overs. "We weren't quick enough to adapt to the conditions.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

"We'd talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here - it's a bit like batting on a trampoline, so there's certain shots which are very difficult to execute. We talked a lot bout trying to put those away.

"We also looked at the history of some of the games here. I think the last four have all been over within about 30-odd overs; we knew we'd be in for a low-scoring contest but we expected to get a few more runs that 131.

"Overall, we're obviously disappointed. But there's some good lessons for us as well - looking towards the World Cup in Africa, there are going to be some pitches there that will also test us with the bounce, and we're going to have to find ways to counter that."

As McCullum suggested, the average first-innings total in the four prior ODIs played at the Optus Stadium is 172, albeit one of those was a weather-affected 26-overs-a-side clash.

A score closer to 200 might well have been competitive on the bouncey, pacey Perth pitch. Instead they collapsed to 65-8 - 21-year-old fast bowler Mahli Beardman starring with 6-24 on debut - before Will Jacks (25) and Gus Atkinson (29no) lifted the tourists' total somewhat.

"Going to Perth as an Englishman is always a bit of a nightmare, the pace and the bounce is very different," former England wicketkeeper Matt Prior said on TNT Sports.

"You've got to have the ability to adapt, which the England batsmen didn't do.

"And you add that to Mahli Beardman having the most incredible day on debut. When you come up against someone you haven't seen a lot of, it can add another challenge.

"Also, one of the big criticisms this ODI batting lineup have had is they only have one gear, which is all-out attack.

"Today was an opportunity to assess the conditions and maybe come down a few gears, bat the full 50 overs and put a score on the board to keep us in the game - the wicket wasn't easy to bat on."

Prior added: "Another thing I picked up on, which is slightly concerning, is England have spoken about their preparation and have made a real point about how well they've prepared this time and the intensity they've trained with.

"They've had 10 days over in Australia, on a surface [at the WACA] that was very similar to the one they played on today, and they've spoken at length about adapting to conditions, and yet that still hasn't materialised in the middle.

"You can have all the team meetings you want, but if you can't take it from the dressing room out into the middle, that is a problem.

"There's quite a bit of work to be done with that batting group around decision making under pressure."

With the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia just under a year away, England have a finite amount of time to correct their issues in the 50-over format.

Currently positioned eighth in the world rankings, Harry Brook's side at least appeared to be trending in the right direction with consecutive series wins in Sri Lanka and at home to India and Sri Lanka in 2026, until losing four of their last five to span a disappointing tri-series in Pakistan and this latest defeat in Australia.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

In the 50-over format, and with the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa less than a year away, England's ODI cricket has largely been trending in the right direction this year until their tri-series troubles in Pakistan in October.

"Like we say winning is a habit, so too is losing. They are going to have to shift it around," Prior said, looking ahead to the second ODI in Adelaide on Sunday and third in Hobart on Wednesday.

"Going to Australia is a tough ask for any any England cricket team, in any format. Coming back from behind is even tougher. It's going to be a massive challenge.

"You're trying to develop the team and learn what your best 11 is, at the same time, so there's a huge amount to contend with. But, this is a performance industry and nothing bloods a team better than actually winning. England need to start that habit."

ODIs 3.30am UK time, with T20s 8.15am UK time

Named after Diego Maradona, Diego Demme helped Napoli win their first Scudetto in the post-Maradona era

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Few players have transformed a club as Diego Maradona did for Napoli. After winning two trophies in their first six decades, Napoli won five in six seasons with Maradona. Maradona's face still adorns the city walls today, and his legacy is etched into the hearts of Napoli supporters like Enzo Demme.

Enzo was seven when he left Italy for Germany, carving out a playing career that took him as high as the 3. Bundesliga. Despite living in Germany, he never stopped supporting Napoli or idolizing Maradona. Even as he was serving a 15-month suspension for cocaine, Demme paid homage to Maradona by naming his son Diego.

Diego followed in Enzo's footballing footsteps with Arminia Bielefeld and Paderborn before spurring RB Leipzig from the third tier to the Champions League. However, silverware eluded the Leipzig captain, whose closest brush with glory ended in defeat to Bayern Munich in the 2018/19 DFB-Pokal Final.

With Leipzig sitting atop the Bundesliga and challenging for their maiden championship, Demme made the surprising decision to join a Napoli side in crisis in January 2020. He established himself as a midfield linchpin, winning the 2019/20 Coppa Italia and ending their six-year trophy drought.

After claiming their fourth trophy of the post-Maradona era, Demme helped Napoli go from seventh to fifth to third to first in Serie A, winning the 2022/23 Scudetto with five games remaining. Unlike in 2020, when COVID-19 restrictions kept supporters apart, Napoli fans could finally take to the streets and celebrate their team's triumph together.

"We won at Udinese and flew back to Napoli, and the whole airport was closed because there were too many people at the airport," stated Demme in an exclusive FourFourTwo interview. "We went to the military airport, and there were still so many people."

Napoli fans had spent 33 years wondering whether the sun would shine on them again after Maradona. 30 months after Maradona's untimely passing, they had finally found their answer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I can't explain the sensation of winning the Scudetto, because it was unbelievable. We were driving from the airport, and behind the bus, there were 200 scooters in the tunnel. They were next to each other, and there was no space, and everybody was celebrating. I was like, ‘Wow, if something happens, then there will be a domino effect, and everyone will fall."

For Enzo, it was the culmination of a lifelong love affair with Napoli. Having watched from afar as Maradona inspired their first Scudetti in 1987 and 1990, he could finally celebrate the title in Naples alongside the son he'd named after his footballing hero.

"My father was crying because it was so emotional for him, because of the whole Maradona story and the Scudetto," added Demme. "Today, when I see the pictures, I think of how wonderful it was. It was a crazy night. We were celebrating with the whole city, and it was great."

Diego Demme, in Herford geboren, hat seinen Vornamen, weil sein Vater Maradona- und Napoli-Fan ist. Schon beim Wechsel aus Leipzig zur SSC Neapel war ein bisschen Familienromantik dabei. Jetzt dürfte Vater Enzo stolz wie Bolle sein. https://t.co/Pq1gHNn7u0May 5, 2023

For a man who had spent nearly his entire life away from Italy, it was a poignant homecoming. The seven-year-old boy who had carried his adoration for Napoli across the Alps had lived long enough to see his son restore his team to the promised land.

Demme left the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in 2024, spending two years at Hertha Berlin before retiring last month. He's still keeping his Napoli roots alive as the co-owner of two Neapolitan pizzerias in Berlin, and he plans to open another in Tbilisi with ex-teammate Khvicha Kvaratshkelia.

Three decades after being named after Napoli's greatest hero, Diego Demme has come full circle. Football brought him back to his father's homeland, and even after hanging up his boots, he's ensuring that a slice of Naples will always remain with him.

#1048. When will Mauricio Pochettino take charge of Manchester United?

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Pochettino has been confirmed as Michael Carrick’s replacement will be in situ for the Premier League trip to Anfield

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United manager just three months into the new season with the club sitting 18th in the Premier League table.

The Old Trafford hierarchy pulled the trigger on Carrick’s departure on Thursday morning after three days of speculation following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa which proved to be Carrick’s final match in charge.

Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager Mauricio Pochettino has reached an agreement with Man United and will become the new head coach.

Pochettino is the current manager of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) but when will he officially begin his tenure at Old Trafford?

Man United’s next match comes on Sunday 22 November when they travel to Anfield to take on Liverpool. It will arguably be the most difficult start possible for whoever takes over and it is a game United need to take something from or else they risk dropping further into the relegation zone.

The current international break would usually provide a new manager with time to train and see the squad in action but Pochettino, should he be given the job, is unlikely to have such a luxury.

That is because the United States have two Nations League matches to play on November 14 and 18 during this window and Pochettino is likely to oversee both fixtures.

The Argentine is still contracted to US Soccer until the 2030 World Cup though an early departure from his deal has now been confirmed. United have made contact with US Soccer over paying compensation to release Pochettino with rumoured figures reaching as high a $10m (£7.4m).

It has also been confirmed that Pochettino will lead the USMNT for their two fixtures with Haiti before flying to Manchester and reporting at Carrington shortly afterwards.

He will be in post at Man United as early as Wednesday 18 November though given the time difference between the US and the UK, Pochettino would arrive late in the afternoon or early evening.

United’s international players are due to return for training on Thursday 19 and Pochettino will oversee his first training session with the club.

That gives him three full days, Thursday 19, Friday 20 and Saturday 21 to settle into his new environment and have time on the grass with the squad.

Whether three days will be enough for the Argentine to inspire a new manager bounce out of United’s playing group remains to be seen.

The new Man United head coach praised US Soccer in the announcement of his departure

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Mauricio Pochettino has offered his heartfelt thanks to US Soccer of the opportunity to coach the national team ahead of his move to Manchester United.

The Argentine was confirmed as the new head coach at Old Trafford on Friday afternoon following the sacking of Michael Carrick the previous day.

US Soccer also announced his departure from his role as head coach of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and revealed that his last two games in charge with be the back-to-back fixtures against Haiti on November 14 and 18.

Pochettino thanked US Soccer for providing him with the chance to take the USA team forward and he revealed that the team will ‘always have a special place’ in his heart.

"The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honours of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country,” Pochettino said in a statement confirming his departure from the role.

“We want to thank Cindy Parlow Cone, JT Batson and Dan Helfrich for their partnership and incredible working relationships throughout our time here.

“There is tremendous talent in the US player pool from the youth teams through to the senior team, and it’s one of the reasons we have so much belief for the future of US Soccer. You will always have a special place in our hearts, and we will be supporting the teams whenever they step on the field."

US Soccer’s CEO and Secretary General JT Batson also praised Pochettino’s work and leadership saying he will lave a ‘lasting mark’ on the team.

“Mauricio has left a lasting mark on US Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture,” said Batson. “What we are most proud of goes beyond the wins.

”He and his staff raised standards, strengthened our culture and created clearer connections from the Youth National Teams to the senior team. Those changes are now embedded in how we operate, and we will keep building on them as we pursue sustained success on the world stage.”

Pochettino took charge of the USMNT in September 2024 and oversaw a record of 21 wins, 12 losses and two draws across 35 matches. In his tenure, the United States reached the 2025 Concacaf Gold Cup Final and advanced to the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup last summer. With three victories during the tournament, Pochettino recorded the most World Cup wins of any head coach in USMNT history.

He will fly to Manchester next week and take up his role as head coach of Man United ahead of the Premier League clash with Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

#1045. Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.
